title: A supported protocol range, capabilities that are read, and a re-check on reconnect
description:
Give the client a real supported RANGE, read the capabilities it already
decodes, and stop assuming the version it saw at connect is the version it is
still talking to.

Today (in the lifted client, protocol.go:31,41,52): ProtocolVersion,
MinProtocolVersion and ProtocolWarnVersion are ALL 20. The supported range is a
single point, so an older herdr is refused outright and a newer one warns on
every connect. That is the structural cause of upgrade breakage in both
directions.

Also today:
- Capabilities are decoded and never read. ServerCapabilities{LiveHandoff,
  DetachedServerDaemon} (types.go:85-88) is referenced nowhere outside a test,
  so every feature is assumed present.
- The check happens ONCE, in New (client.go:107). SessionSnapshot carries a
  protocol field (types.go:231) that no production code reads. A herdr that
  restarts under a different version mid-run is never re-checked.

Do:
- Separate the three constants into what they actually mean: the oldest protocol
  this client can speak, the newest it was verified against, and the newest it
  will speak without a warning. Support a RANGE, with no upper bound — an
  unknown-but-newer server proceeds.
- Branch on capabilities rather than assuming. A feature the server does not
  advertise is refused BY NAME at the point of use, not discovered as a failure.
- Re-check on every reconnect, and read the protocol field the snapshot already
  carries. A version change mid-run must be noticed.
- A version or capability refusal is OPERATIONAL. It must never reject a tick or
  tear an attempt down — see the never-a-verdict tick, which owns the tests.
- Distinguish "herdr is not running" from "herdr is the wrong version". Today
  both flatten to one generic exit (herd_shared.go:21-27).

acceptance_criteria: Floor, verified-against and warn are three distinct values and a newer-than-verified server proceeds without refusal; a capability the server does not advertise is refused by name at the point of use rather than failing later; the protocol is re-checked on reconnect and the snapshot's protocol field is read; 'herdr is not running' and 'herdr is the wrong version' are distinguishable at the exit; tests cover a server below the floor, above the warn version, one missing a capability, and one that changes version mid-run; go test -short -timeout 45m ./... green.
closed_reason: A real protocol range: floor 19, verified 20, warn 22, with by-name capability refusal, a mid-run re-check, and 'not running' distinguished from 'wrong version'. Verified against a LIVE herdr 0.9.0 on protocol 22 and recorded the 19-to-20 shape diff as additive. Wave gate green (EXIT=0, reconcile 710s).
